cards.heading: Autonomous APs
cards.body: An autonomous AP is configured and managed on its own, like a small switch with a radio. Fine for a few APs; every AP's VLANs must be trunked to it.

cards.heading: Lightweight APs and the WLC
cards.body: In split-MAC architecture, lightweight APs handle the real-time radio work (beacons, acknowledgements, encryption) while a wireless LAN controller handles management, authentication, roaming and RF tuning. They talk over CAPWAP tunnels: UDP 5246 for control (encrypted with DTLS) and UDP 5247 for data.

cards.heading: Cloud-based APs
cards.body: Cloud-managed APs (such as Meraki) are configured and monitored from a cloud dashboard. User data stays local; only management goes to the cloud.

cards.heading: AP modes
cards.body: Local: the default; serves clients and tunnels their traffic to the WLC. FlexConnect: switches client traffic locally at a branch and keeps working if the WLC link fails. Monitor: doesn't serve clients; scans for rogues and intrusions. Sniffer: captures 802.11 frames for analysis. Rogue detector: listens on the wire for rogue devices. SE-Connect: spectrum analysis of interference. Bridge/mesh: links APs wirelessly.

cards.heading: Switch ports for APs
cards.body: A lightweight AP in local mode only needs an access port: its traffic is tunnelled to the WLC. An autonomous AP or a FlexConnect AP switching several VLANs locally needs a trunk.

cards.heading: WLC ports and interfaces
cards.body: Physical ports: the service port (out-of-band management), distribution system ports (to the switched network, usually trunks bundled with LAG), the console port and the redundancy port (to a standby WLC). Logical interfaces: management (and AP management), virtual (DHCP relay, web auth), service-port, and dynamic interfaces that map each WLAN to a VLAN. WLC LAG doesn't negotiate, so the switch must use channel-group mode on.
cards.example:
interface range g1/0/1 - 2
 channel-group 1 mode on
interface port-channel 1
 switchport mode trunk

cards.heading: Creating a WLAN in the GUI
cards.body: WLANs > Create New: give a profile name, the SSID and a WLAN ID. General tab: enable it and pick the interface (VLAN) its clients use. Security tab: Layer 2 security such as WPA2 with a PSK or 802.1X. QoS tab: Platinum (voice), Gold (video), Silver (best effort, default) or Bronze (background). Advanced tab: options such as FlexConnect local switching and session timeouts.
